:::{#exm-newton-quadratic}
#### One step to the minimizer

Let $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2} (x_1^2 + 3 x_2^2)$, so $\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 }$ and $\vecf{c} = \vzero_{2 \times 1}$.
From $\vx^{(0)} = \tp{(3, 1)}$ the gradient is $\matr{S} \vx^{(0)} = \tp{(3, 3)}$,
and $\matr{S}^{-1} = \sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1/3 }$, so the Newton step is
$-\matr{S}^{-1} \tp{(3, 3)} = -\tp{(3, 1)}$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vx^{(1)} &= \tp{(3, 1)} - \tp{(3, 1)} \\
&= \vzero_{2 \times 1},
\end{aligned}
$$

the minimizer.

@fig-newton-quadratic shows the step on the [level curves](vector-calculus.qmd#def-level-set) of $f$.

{{< include mds/_subfiles/vector-calc/_fig-newton-quadratic.qmd >}}

@fig-newton-quadratic-3d shows the same [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function) as a surface.

{{< include mds/_subfiles/vector-calc/_fig-newton-quadratic-3d.qmd >}}

:::
